case_file.goal: Run the Node/Express API in Docker with docker compose; it works with `npm run dev` on the laptop but crashes on startup inside the container.
case_file.symptom:
PrismaClientInitializationError: Prisma Client could not locate the Query Engine for runtime "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x".

This happened because Prisma Client was generated for "darwin-arm64", but the actual deployment required "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x".
Add "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x" to `binaryTargets` in the "schema.prisma" file and run `prisma generate` after saving it:

generator client {
  provider      = "prisma-client-js"
  binaryTargets = ["native", "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x"]
}

The following locations have been searched:
  /app/node_modules/.prisma/client
  /app/node_modules/@prisma/client
    at Ln (/app/node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/library.js:111:9)
    at async Object.loadLibrary (/app/node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/library.js:111:2134)
case_file.environment: macOS 15 on Apple Silicon (darwin-arm64) for development; Docker image node:20-alpine (Alpine 3.20, musl, OpenSSL 3); Node 20.18; prisma 5.22.0, @prisma/client 5.22.0; PostgreSQL 16 in a second compose service.

tried.attempt: Deleted node_modules and ran npm ci again on the laptop, then rebuilt the image
Ran `npx prisma generate` on the laptop before docker compose build
tried.result: Same error, still says generated for darwin-arm64

final.message:
TEAM_REPORT: run tr_demo5a1c0e9b. 3 likely cause(s), most likely first. Try them one at a time on the real project and rerun the check after each.

1. [86% confidence] The laptop's node_modules is copied into the image. .dockerignore doesn't exclude it, so COPY . . replaces the Prisma Client that npm ci built in the container with one generated for darwin-arm64, which has no Alpine (musl) engine.
   found by: docs, issues, community
   evidence (docs): https://docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context/#dockerignore-files - "Use a .dockerignore file to exclude files and directories from the build context."
   evidence (github): https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/1642 - "generate the client inside the container, not on your machine"
   evidence (community): https://station.railway.com/questions/prisma-suddenly-crashes-on-today-s-deplo-1d3c525f - "Add the target the deployment needs to binaryTargets and run prisma generate again"
   steps:
     1. Add node_modules to .dockerignore (next to .git, .env and dist).
     2. Rebuild without the cached layers: docker compose build --no-cache api.
   check: run `docker compose up --build api` (The api service logs 'listening on :3000' and stays up.)

2. [64% confidence] Nothing generates the client for Alpine inside the image: binaryTargets has no musl target, and npm ci --omit=dev leaves out the prisma CLI, so prisma generate never runs in the container.
   found by: docs, issues
   evidence (docs): https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-schema-reference#binarytargets-options - "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x: Alpine Linux 3.17+ (x86_64)"
   evidence (github): https://github.com/prisma/prisma/discussions/702 - "add the musl binary target and run prisma generate in the Dockerfile"
   steps:
     1. In prisma/schema.prisma, set binaryTargets = ["native", "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x"] in the generator client block.
     2. In the Dockerfile, run npm ci (with dev dependencies), then COPY . ., then npx prisma generate and npm run build.
     3. Finish the Dockerfile with npm prune --omit=dev to drop dev dependencies from the final image.
   check: run `docker compose up --build api` (The api service logs 'listening on :3000' and stays up.)

3. [31% confidence] OpenSSL isn't installed in the Alpine image, so Prisma can't detect libssl and picks no engine even when the right one is there.
   found by: community
   evidence (community): https://station.railway.com/questions/error-with-prisma-open-ssl-259588ed - "apk add --no-cache openssl in the Dockerfile fixed it"
   evidence (community): https://zenn.dev/gtca/scraps/8e53ee95ad57c0 - "Prisma failed to detect the libssl/openssl version to use"
   steps:
     1. Add RUN apk add --no-cache openssl to the Dockerfile, before npm ci.
   check: run `docker compose run --rm api npx prisma -v` (Lists linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x as the platform, with no libssl warning.)

Setup check: Development is on darwin-arm64; the image is node:20-alpine (Alpine 3.20, musl, OpenSSL 3), which needs Prisma's linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x engine. Prisma 5.22 supports it.

If none work: Run docker compose run --rm api npx prisma -v and compare the engine platform with the image. If it still says darwin-arm64, a host-built client is still being copied in: check every COPY line and the .dockerignore.

Possible answer: untested suggestions from web research. The server can't run the check, so try each one on the real project; it only counts as solved once the check passes.
